rulings.challenge_claim: The frame-opening span is argued without touching the bytes that close the preceding frame - the colophon and the parashah mark standing on the verse immediately before its onset - and its name-spelling digit reasons from four verses outside the span that carry no matching evidence ref.
rulings.grounds: Two distinct defects, both byte-confirmed. First, the onset's immediate predecessor closes with עַד הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.51.64, byte tier) - a colophon, which the evidence policy ranks tier-1 and which is the strongest available warrant for an appendix onset standing right after it; the span's prose engages neither that run nor the setumah carried by the same verse (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak in the Prophets; absence never counterevidence). The mark-disclosure symmetry contract is unconditional over the front-seam verse before the span's first verse, its interior, and its end verse, so this mark sits inside the span-relevant set by definition and the declared false-positive disposition on the gap does not survive its own contract. The warrant the span does use is a regnal age-at-accession formula, which the book's device catalogue keeps outside the dated-header object - so the onset stands on the weaker of the two signals available at this seam while the stronger one goes uncited. Second, the name digit's object and count are both right - the long spelling צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ (oshb:Jer.52.1, byte tier) stands in six verses of this chapter, 52:1, 52:3, 52:5, 52:8, 52:10, 52:11 (sweep: 6 verses) - but four of the six verses enumerated in prose lie outside Jer.52.1-Jer.52.3 while the evidence refs stop at oshb:Jer.52.3, and a bare verse enumeration argued in prose is still a verse argued from outside the span.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: cite the colophon run at oshb:Jer.51.64 (byte tier) as the tier-1 signal closing the preceding frame immediately before this onset, alongside the accession formula already quoted. device_notes: disclose the setumah at oshb:Jer.51.64 (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak corroboration under the Prophets addendum; not a driver, absence never counterevidence). boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.51.64; and either add oshb:Jer.52.5, oshb:Jer.52.8, oshb:Jer.52.10, oshb:Jer.52.11 or restate the device_notes digit with the sweep shorthand alone, enumerating no out-of-span verse. Test the cure must pass: the span-relevant mark sweep (front-seam verse before the span, interior, end verse) returns no undisclosed mark for this span, and every verse named or enumerated anywhere in the row's prose outside Jer.52.1-Jer.52.3 resolves to an entry in boundary_evidence_refs.

rulings.challenge_claim: The stated ground for holding Jer.52.4-Jer.52.11 whole - that no fresh date breaks the chain - is contested by 52:6, which opens its verse with a month-and-day dating notice in the same shape treated as boundary-bearing at 52:12.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed. Jer 52:6 opens בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי֙ בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ (oshb:Jer.52.6, byte tier): month ordinal plus day, verse-initial and asyndetic, with the famine clause following it; the span quotes and disposition nothing from that verse. The boundary drawn at Jer.52.12 rests on וּבַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַֽחֲמִישִׁי֙ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ (oshb:Jer.52.12, byte tier) - the same month-and-day shape carrying only a prefixed vav and a mid-verse year gloss. The span does clear the weaker shape at 52:5 explicitly and correctly, עַ֚ד עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.52.5, byte tier) being a terminus rather than an onset, which makes the silence over the stronger verse-initial shape at 52:6 an asymmetry inside the same class rather than a uniform decision about it. The 52:6 notice carries no year word, so it is invisible to a year-token sweep - that explains the omission but does not license the categorical wording, which as written is falsified by a dating notice standing inside the span. The English paragraph break at that verse is tier-4 and carries no weight in either direction. What is upheld is the wording defect only: whether 52:6 should cut is not decided here, since its date sits inside the siege the 52:4 frame opens, and whether a yearless verse-initial month-and-day notice belongs to the ruled date-onset class is a definitional question the granularity ruling does not settle.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative and boundary_rationale: replace the categorical no-fresh-date wording with a per-site reading that names oshb:Jer.52.6, quotes its verse-initial month-and-day run at byte tier, and states why it is read as internal to the siege the 52:4 frame opens - the same per-site treatment the row already gives the terminus at 52:5. device_notes: name the shape and its year-word absence. boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.52.6. Test the cure must pass: no categorical claim about dates survives in the row that a dating notice standing inside Jer.52.4-Jer.52.11 falsifies, and every date-shaped verse inside the span is dispositioned per-site with its bytes quoted. A cut at 52:6 is a boundary proposal requiring explicit adoption, never author work under this remedy.

rulings.challenge_claim: One side: the closing seam at 52:16/17 rests on a bare change of narrated object rather than a disclosed tier-1 device, the high rating is optimistic, and an in-span paseq goes undisclosed. Other side: the cohesion clause folds 52:14 under the newly named captain of the guard although that verse predicates its action of the Chaldean army, no Hebrew is engaged from 52:13-52:15, the same paseq goes undisclosed, and the contrast drawn against a verse-initial shape is mislabelled.
rulings.grounds: All four components verify on bytes; the paseq item is the SAME defect on both sides, the seam item and the agent item are DISTINCT. Seam: no speech formula, word-event formula, or dating notice stands at the following verse, which opens וְאֶת עַמּוּדֵ֨י הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת (oshb:Jer.52.17, byte tier) with שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים (oshb:Jer.52.17, byte tier) as its predicate - a change of narrated object with no tier-1 device disclosed, under a high rating and no frontier flag. Agent: 52:14 predicates its wall-breaking of נָֽתְצוּ֙ כָּל חֵ֣יל כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים (oshb:Jer.52.14, byte tier), the captain of the guard entering only inside the relative clause that follows, so the span's own claim that what the newly named agent does under that dating stays one span is byte-false at the middle of the span - the acting subject alternates across 52:13 (singular), 52:14 (the Chaldean army) and 52:15-52:16 (the named captain). Engagement: the span quotes Hebrew from 52:12 and 52:16 only, so the stretch carrying the contested cohesion claim is asserted rather than shown. Disclosure: a paseq stands at oshb:Jer.52.15 (single-witness WLC; seg layer; count-only, no position sourceable) inside the span and is undisclosed, while the same layer is disclosed at oshb:Jer.52.3 and oshb:Jer.52.25 elsewhere in this chapter - an omission, not a policy. Wording: the 52:12 notice is itself verse-initial, וּבַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַֽחֲמִישִׁי֙ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ (oshb:Jer.52.12, byte tier), so the real contrast against the 52:4 frame is year-first against month-first, not verse-initial against anything. One further gap neither item names: the bare-title recurrence claim carries neither digit nor tier while the name claim beside it carries the sweep shorthand - the title stands in eight verses of this chapter, three of them without the name (52:14, 52:19, 52:24).
rulings.remedy: device_notes: disclose the paseq at oshb:Jer.52.15 (single-witness WLC, count-only, position not recorded); give the bare-title recurrence its digit and unit on the same convention the name claim already uses. boundary_rationale: replace the one-agent cohesion clause with the byte reading that the acting subject alternates across 52:13, 52:14 and 52:15-52:16, quoting the predicate from 52:14; correct the date contrast to year-first against month-first; and either disclose a tier-1 device at the 52:16/17 seam - the fronted vav-plus-object run beginning there is a list/register shape and is available - or lower confidence from high and set frontier_flag_considered true. strongest_rejected_alternative: weigh holding the destruction and deportation report together with the bronze catalogue that follows, not only the internal options. Test the cure must pass: every cohesion claim about an acting agent is carried by a quoted predicate from the verse it covers; every disclosure object inside Jer.52.12-Jer.52.16 appears in the prose; and the confidence rating survives the question of which tier-1 device stands at the closing seam. Any respan is a proposal requiring explicit adoption.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both seams of this span rest on a change of catalogued object rather than a disclosed tier-1 device - the fronted construction and the subject change relied on at 52:17 already stand inside the preceding stretch, and no participant newly enters at 52:23/24 - while confidence is declared high, and the in-span paseq goes undisclosed although a ketiv/qere in the same span is engaged.
rulings.grounds: Same defect from two sides at the 52:17 seam, plus one shared disclosure gap, plus the second seam raised on one side only; all components verify. 52:17 opens וְאֶת עַמּוּדֵ֨י הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת and predicates שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים (oshb:Jer.52.17, byte tier); the same fronted vav-plus-object construction with the same subject class already stands at 52:14, וְאֶת כָּל חֹמ֥וֹת ... נָֽתְצוּ֙ כָּל חֵ֣יל כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים (oshb:Jer.52.14, byte tier), where no cut is made, and the acting subject alternates 52:14, 52:15-52:16, 52:17 - so neither the construction nor a subject change distinguishes this seam from points inside the preceding stretch. At the other seam the agent is not new either: 52:24 opens וַיִּקַּ֣ח רַב טַבָּחִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.52.24, byte tier) under a title that has already acted at 52:19, לָקַ֖ח רַב טַבָּחִֽים (oshb:Jer.52.19, byte tier). No dating notice and no speech formula stands at either seam. A paseq stands at oshb:Jer.52.20 (single-witness WLC, count-only, no position sourceable) - inside the verse quoted at length - and is undisclosed, while the ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.52.21 is engaged in the same field; that ketiv/qere description matches the bytes, and the cardinal-teen reading at 52:20 is right in its object, a count of oxen rather than a year. The span's own notes concede an unresolved agency question between 52:17 and 52:19 while confidence stands at high with the frontier flag unset. Corrected framing for the cure: a tier-1 register warrant is undisclosed rather than absent - 52:17, 52:18 and 52:19 each open with a fronted vav-plus-object accusative and the run closes on the summing clause לֹא הָיָ֣ה מִשְׁקָ֔ל לִנְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם כָּל הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Jer.52.20, byte tier), while 52:21-52:23 are measurement clauses with no narrative progression against the resumed narrative verb at 52:24. So the cure is disclosure and a matching confidence, not a respan.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: disclose at each seam the device actually carried by the bytes - the fronted vav-plus-object run at 52:17, 52:18, 52:19 closed by the summing clause at 52:20 as a list/register onset, and the measurement clauses of 52:21-52:23 against the resumed narrative verb at 52:24 - quoting the runs at byte tier; absent that disclosure, lower confidence to medium_low and set frontier_flag_considered true. device_notes: disclose the paseq at oshb:Jer.52.20 (single-witness WLC, count-only, position not recorded) beside the ketiv/qere already engaged at oshb:Jer.52.21, and either resolve the agency question the notes raise or state it as held open with the bytes for both agents quoted. strongest_rejected_alternative: engage the outer-seam rival - holding this catalogue with the destruction report before it, or with the officials' seizure after it - rather than only the internal split. Test the cure must pass: no seam in the row is warranted by a change of narrated object alone; the warrant offered at each seam is one the preceding stretch does not equally satisfy; every disclosure object inside Jer.52.17-Jer.52.23 appears in the prose; and the confidence rating is defensible against a reader who asks which tier-1 device stands at each seam. Any respan is a proposal requiring explicit adoption.

rulings.challenge_claim: One side: the opening seam at 52:23/24 rests on a bare change of narrated object, with no new agent entering and no one newly addressed, so the participant-shift reading overstates the bytes and the high rating is optimistic. Other side: the closure argument reads the Judah token at 52:27 as the same named land the chapter's opening makes the scene, but the bytes give the token two different roles and name a different word for the land, and 52:3 is argued from outside the span with no matching evidence ref.
rulings.grounds: Two distinct defects, both byte-confirmed. Onset: 52:24 opens וַיִּקַּ֣ח רַב טַבָּחִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.52.24, byte tier) under a title that has already acted at 52:19, לָקַ֖ח רַב טַבָּחִֽים (oshb:Jer.52.19, byte tier), so no participant newly enters; and no addressee exists anywhere in this chapter to shift - not one of its 34 verses opens a quoted-speech run (sweep: 0 of 34 verses carry a quotation-opening mark, against the quoted oracle standing at 51:64), and the chapter's two speech verbs, at 52:9 and 52:32, report speech without any addressed content. That makes the addressee-shift signal key a label the span's bytes do not instantiate; the same key also stands on the span covering Jer.52.12-Jer.52.16. Closure: 52:27 closes וַיִּ֥גֶל יְהוּדָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.52.27, byte tier) - Judah is the exiled entity and the land is the suffixed noun, not the toponym - while at 52:3 the same token stands inside the locative pair בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.52.3, byte tier) belonging to the divine-anger clause, the rebellion clause of that verse naming only the king and the king of Babylon; so naming one land as the scene of both the rebellion and the exile is not what either verse says. That claim also argues 52:3 in prose from outside the span while the evidence refs reach only to oshb:Jer.52.23 on that side. The rest holds: the office-against-role contrast drawn at 52:24 and 52:25 is byte-true, the paseq at oshb:Jer.52.25 is disclosed (single-witness WLC, count-only), and no ketiv/qere and no parashah mark falls inside Jer.52.24-Jer.52.27. One precision the bytes add to the onset item: the captain of the guard is the continuously present commissioning figure but not the continuous grammatical subject, since 52:14 and 52:17 predicate their actions of the Chaldeans - which strengthens rather than weakens the finding that nothing newly enters at this seam.
rulings.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: drop the addressee-shift key and replace it with one the span's bytes instantiate - the resumed narrative verb after the measurement clauses of 52:21-52:23, with a register of named and counted officials - and re-open the fields a signal swap makes dependent (boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type, confidence). boundary_rationale: either disclose a tier-1 device at the 52:23/24 seam or lower confidence from high and set frontier_flag_considered true. device_notes: re-cut the echo sentence to the roles the bytes carry - Judah as the exiled entity at 52:27 with the land as the suffixed noun, against the locative pair inside the anger clause at 52:3 - or drop it; if it is kept, add oshb:Jer.52.3 to boundary_evidence_refs, and note that the byte-true hook between the two verses is the repeated preposition-plus-suffix, מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו (oshb:Jer.52.3, byte tier) against the close of 52:27. strongest_rejected_alternative: weigh holding the bronze catalogue and the officials' seizure together, the rival at the contested seam, not only the forward rival. Test the cure must pass: every signal key names a device the span's own bytes carry; every echo or recurrence claim names the grammatical role each token holds in each verse it cites; and every verse argued in prose outside Jer.52.24-Jer.52.27 appears in boundary_evidence_refs.

rulings.challenge_claim: The onset frame is misdescribed: the verse-initial date reckons by the Judean king's exile, not by a Babylonian king's accession, and the accession reading rests on an ordinal the Hebrew does not carry.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed. The verse-initial frame reads בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ן מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.52.31, byte tier) - thirty-seven years reckoned to the exile of the king of Judah. The Babylonian reckoning is a separate mid-verse element, בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מַלְכֻת֗וֹ (oshb:Jer.52.31, byte tier), and no ordinal token stands with it, so “in the first year of his reign” (web:Jer.52.31) is supplied by the English rendering. Describing the opening frame as dated to a Babylonian king's own accession therefore states of the verse-initial frame what the bytes place mid-verse, and adds a digit only the rendering carries; the same wording is reused as the ground for not folding the notice back into the preceding census, so the defect is load-bearing rather than decorative. The verse also carries two date elements, not one, so a single verse-initial signal does not describe its shape completely. A further defect in the same sentence that the challenge does not name: the interval claim placing this notice decades after the totals just given is not sourceable from the verses cited - the census entries count Nebuchadnezzar's regnal years while this onset counts from a Judean king's exile and from a reign-year phrase carrying no ordinal, so the two reckonings are not commensurable on these bytes; the claim is not shown false, but the only thing that would bridge them is an outside parallel, which is typed-relation metadata and never decides a seam here. The boundary itself is not contested and the rest verifies: the two spellings of the king's name inside 52:31 are byte-real and both belong to the same name form, neither the Jeconiah nor the Coniah form; the ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.52.31 and at oshb:Jer.52.32 each stand as a single note in the inventory, so no ordinal ranking between them is asserted or needed; the petuchah at oshb:Jer.52.30 is correctly typed and framed as tier-3 weak, single-witness.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: restate the onset frame as the bytes carry it - verse-initial, thirty-seven years to the exile of the king of Judah - and name the Babylonian reign-year element as a separate mid-verse element carrying no ordinal; wherever the rendering's first-year wording is relied on, mark it as the English rendering's supplement rather than a byte fact. strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the accession-year ground with one the bytes carry - a fresh verse-initial dated frame on a different reckoning plus a scene change to Babylon - and drop the decades-interval clause unless it can be sourced from within these two witnesses. device_notes: record that this verse carries two date elements, not one. Test the cure must pass: no boundary ground states of a verse-initial frame what the bytes place mid-verse, and no digit or interval survives in the row that only the English rendering or an out-of-book parallel supplies.
